section.heading: Review of operation of amendments made by Schedule 1

content.p: The Minister must cause an independent review to be conducted of the operation of the amendments made by Schedule 1 to this Act.
Timing of review
The persons conducting the review must complete the review before the end of the period of 2 years starting on the day this section commences.
Minister to be given report of review
The persons conducting the review must give the Minister a written report of the review as soon as practicable after the review is completed.
Minister to table copy of report of review
The Minister must cause a copy of the report of the review to be tabled in each House of the Parliament within 15 sitting days of that House after the Minister receives the report.

content.p: This section applies in relation to a registered provider if:
the provider is not an approved school provider; and

section.heading: Minister may make instrument specifying courses

content.p: The Minister may, by legislative instrument, specify one or more classes of courses for the purposes of this section if the Minister is satisfied on reasonable grounds that:
there are or have been systemic problems in relation to the standard of delivery of the courses included in the class; or
the courses included in the class provide limited value to Australia’s current, emerging and future skills and training needs and priorities; or
it is in the public interest to do so.
In considering whether to make such an instrument, the Minister must have regard to all of the following matters:
whether the courses included in the class are provided by registered providers that are breaching or have breached:
this Act; or
the national code; or
if the ELICOS Standards or Foundation Program Standards apply in relation to the provider—those Standards; or
a condition of the provider’s registration;
completion rates of accepted students of those courses;
the number of transfers of accepted students from or to those courses;
the location or locations at which providers are registered to provide those courses.
Subsection (2) does not limit the matters to which the Minister may have regard in considering whether to make an instrument under subsection (1).
Specified courses
Without limiting subsection (1) or any other provision of this Act, a class of courses may be specified by reference to any matter, including, but not limited to, any of the following:
the kind of course;
the kind of provider registered to provide the course;
the location of the course;
any other circumstances applying in relation to the course.
Prescribing matters by reference to other instruments

section.heading: Application for registration of specified courses taken not to be made

content.p: This section applies if:
(a) a provider (other than a Table A provider within the meaning of the Higher Education Support Act 2003) makes an application under:
section 9 to register a course; or
section 10D to renew the registration of a course; or
section 10H to add a course to the provider’s registration; and

The application is taken not to have been made in relation to the course.
This section applies if:
(a) a registered provider (other than a Table A provider within the meaning of the Higher Education Support Act 2003) is registered to provide a course at a location or locations; and
the course is included in a class of courses specified in an instrument in force under subsection 96B(1); and
30 days after that instrument commences, one or more students are enrolled in and have commenced, but not completed or withdrawn from, the course.
The provider’s registration for the course is suspended for all locations by force of this subsection.
A provider whose registration is suspended for a course under this section must not:
do any thing for the purpose of recruiting or enrolling overseas students or intending overseas students for the course; or
solicit or accept any money from an overseas student or an intending overseas student for the course other than overseas students who are enrolled in and have commenced the course; or
if an accepted student of the provider has not commenced the course—permit the student to commence the course.
The provider is still registered for the course for the location for all other purposes.
This section applies if:
(a) a registered provider (other than a Table A provider within the meaning of the Higher Education Support Act 2003) is registered to provide a course at a location or locations; and
the course is included in a class of courses specified in an instrument in force under subsection 96B(1); and
30 days after that instrument commences, there are no students that are enrolled in and have commenced, but not completed or withdrawn from, the course.
This section also applies if:
a provider’s registration for a course is suspended under section 96D; and
all students that were enrolled in and had commenced the course before the suspension have since completed or withdrawn from the course.
The provider’s registration for the course is cancelled for all locations by force of this subsection.

section.heading: Meaning of offshore provided Australian course of study

content.p: (1) An offshore provided Australian course of study means an Australian course of study that is provided at offshore premises, but does not include a course, or a course included in a class of courses:
covered by subsection (2); or
that the Minister determines under subsection (3) is not an offshore provided Australian course of study.
For the purposes of paragraph (1)(a), each of the following is not an offshore provided Australian course of study:

(a) an Australian course of study with a higher education provider that involves a formal exchange agreement between the provider and another entity that is not in Australia (the offshore entity) that provides for the undertaking of study:
with the offshore entity at an offshore premises; and
for a period of no longer than 12 months; and
that contributes to the requirements of the course of study;
an Australian course of study with a higher education provider that involves the undertaking of research:
not in Australia; and
that contributes to the requirements of the course of study.

For the purposes of paragraph (1)(b), the Minister may, by legislative instrument, determine that a course, or a course included in a class of courses, is not an offshore provided Australian course of study.
Without limiting subsection (3), a class of courses may be determined by reference to any matter, including, but not limited to, any of the following:
the kind of course;
the kind of provider accredited to provide the course;
any other circumstances applying in relation to the course.

A regulated entity who is, or has applied to become, a registered higher education provider may apply to TEQSA for authorisation to offer or confer Australian higher education awards for one or more offshore provided Australian courses of study.
An application must be:
in the approved form; and
accompanied by any information, documents and assistance that TEQSA requests; and
accompanied by the fee (if any) determined under section 158 for an assessment under this Part.
An application may only be made on or after 1 January 2026.
Grant of application for authorisation
TEQSA may grant the application for authorisation if TEQSA is satisfied that:
the applicant is a registered higher education provider; and
the applicant meets the Threshold Standards.
Decision on application
TEQSA must make a decision on the application:
within 9 months of receiving it; or
if a longer period is determined by TEQSA under subsection (3)—within that period.
For the purposes of paragraph (a), if a fee is determined under section 158 for an assessment under this Part, TEQSA is taken to receive the application when it receives payment of the fee.
Longer period for decision on application

If TEQSA is satisfied that, for reasons beyond its control, a decision on the application cannot be made within the period mentioned in paragraph (2)(a), TEQSA may determine a longer period, not exceeding a further 9 months, within which it must make a decision on the application.
If TEQSA determines a longer period, it must do so not later than 6 weeks before the end of the period mentioned in paragraph (2)(a).
If TEQSA determines a longer period, TEQSA must, within 7 days of making the determination:
notify the applicant, in writing, of the determination; and
give, in writing, the reasons for the determination.
Decision not made
TEQSA is taken to have rejected the application if a decision is not made within the period applicable under subsection (2).

section.heading: TEQSA to give notice of decision about authorisation

content.p: TEQSA must, within 30 days of its decision to grant or reject an application for authorisation as an authorised offshore provider, notify the applicant, in writing, of:
the decision; and
if TEQSA grants the application—the day on which the authorisation commences; and
if TEQSA rejects the application—the reasons for the decision.
Note: TEQSA must also notify of any conditions imposed under subsection 44J(1) on the authorisation (see section 44K).
An applicant’s authorisation commences on the day specified in the notice given under section 44D.
The authorisation has effect subject to the following:
the authorisation ends immediately if the provider ceases to be registered as a registered higher education provider;
Division 1 of Part 7 (about cancelling authorisation and other administrative sanctions).
A registered higher education provider must:
comply with the conditions imposed by sections 44G and 44H on the provider’s authorisation as an authorised offshore provider; and
comply with any conditions imposed under subsection 44J(1) on the provider’s authorisation as an authorised offshore provider.

section.heading: Condition—notice about certain events and changes in circumstances must be given

content.p: A registered higher education provider must give TEQSA notice in writing if any of the following events or changes in circumstances occurs or is likely to occur:
an offshore provided Australian course of study provided by the provider first begins to be provided wholly or partly by another entity;
an offshore provided Australian course of study provided by the provider first begins to be provided at a different premises;
the provider first begins to provide an offshore provided Australian course of study;
the provider ceases to provide an Australian offshore provided Australian course of study.
The notice must include the following information:
details of the event or change;
the day the event or change occurs or is likely to occur;
the name of the Australian course of study;
the address of the offshore premises;
if the course is provided by another entity—the name of that entity.
The notice must be given:
as soon as the provider is aware, or would reasonably be expected to have become aware, of the event or change; and
no later than 90 days before the day the event or change occurs or is likely to occur.

An authorised offshore provider must, by 31 October of each calendar year, prepare and give to TEQSA a report that contains information about each offshore provided Australian course of study provided by the provider (including provided wholly or partly by another entity) during the most recently completed academic year for the course of study.
A report under subsection (1) must:
be in a manner (if any) specified in a legislative instrument made under subsection (3); and
contain the information (if any) required by a legislative instrument made under subsection (3).
TEQSA may, by legislative instrument, specify requirements for reports under this section.
TEQSA may impose additional conditions on the authorisation of a provider as an authorised offshore provider.
TEQSA may, on its own initiative, vary or revoke a condition imposed under subsection (1).
TEQSA may also vary or revoke a condition imposed under subsection (1) if the provider applies for the variation or revocation.
The provider’s application must be:
in the approved form; and
accompanied by any information, documents and assistance that TEQSA requests; and
accompanied by the fee (if any) determined under section 158 for an application under this section.

section.heading: TEQSA to notify provider of decision to impose, vary or revoke a condition

content.p: TEQSA must, within 30 days of making a decision under subsection 44J(1), (2) or (3), notify the registered higher education provider, in writing, of:
the decision; and
the reasons for the decision; and
if the decision is to impose a condition—the period for which the condition is imposed.
A registered higher education provider may apply to TEQSA, in the approved form, to withdraw its authorisation.
Upon receiving the provider’s application to withdraw its authorisation, TEQSA may grant the application if TEQSA is satisfied that it is appropriate to allow the authorisation to be withdrawn.

section.heading: TEQSA to notify provider of decision about withdrawal

content.p: TEQSA must, within 30 days of its decision to grant or reject an application to withdraw an authorisation, notify the registered higher education provider, in writing, of:
the decision; and
if TEQSA grants the application—the day on which the withdrawal takes effect; and
if TEQSA rejects the application—the reasons for the decision.

section.heading: Offering a regulated higher education award offshore if not authorised

content.p: Offence
A higher education provider commits an offence if:
the higher education provider offers or confers an Australian higher education award for the completion of an Australian course of study; and
the course of study is an offshore provided Australian course of study; and

A higher education provider contravenes this subsection if:
the higher education provider offers or confers an Australian higher education award for the completion of an Australian course of study; and
the course of study is an offshore provided Australian course of study; and
the higher education provider is not an authorised offshore provider.
Civil penalty: 240 penalty units.
